name: Logic Pro
note: Every row of the "Key command tables" section of Apple's Logic Pro User Guide for Mac (the "Default keyboard shortcuts" pages, read from Apple's own PDF of the guide). Apple splits the tables by area and each area name is used as the context: Global Commands, Global Control Surfaces Commands, Various Windows, Windows Showing Audio Files, Main Window Tracks and Various Editors, Various Editors, Views Showing Time Ruler, Views Showing Automation, Main Window Tracks, Live Loops Grid, Mixer, MIDI Environment, Piano Roll, Score Editor, Event Editor, Step Editor, Step Sequencer, Project Audio, Audio File Editor, Smart Tempo Editor, Sampler, Step Input Keyboard, Smart Controls and Tool Menu. The action name is Apple's own Function column, so it keeps Apple's wording exactly. Apple's table reflects the U.S. default key command preset. Logic Pro is macOS only, so only "mac" is filled in; Apple writes Control, Option and Command, which are written here as Ctrl, Alt and Cmd, and Apple's "Delete (backspace)" is written as Backspace while its "Forward Delete" is Delete. Left out: every row Apple marks with the numeric-keypad glyph (Record/Record Toggle, Play, Pause, Stop, Skip Cycle, Toggle Replace, Go to Marker Number 1-19, Recall Screenset 1-9 and 1x-9x, and the other keypad rows), because the grammar has no numpad keys; and the ten Control Surface Install Window rows whose "shortcut" is a modifier held while launching Logic Pro or while clicking a project in the Finder.
